data.name: Edda
data.gender_notes: Edda is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Norse mythology, Edda is the name of the goddess of poetry and wisdom. She is also the source of the collection of poems known as the Poetic Edda. In Christianity, the name Edda holds no specific religious significance, but it can be seen as a symbol of wisdom and knowledge. The name Edda carries the meaning “Goddess of poetry and wisdom” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Edda usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of poetry and wisdom and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Edda belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of poetry and wisdom.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Edda total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_latin.name: Edda
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Edda originates from Latin roots and signifies a beautiful and pure individual. Historically, the name has been associated with virtues of beauty and purity in Christian tradition.

in_english.name: Edda
in_english.meaning: Edda represents a beautiful and pure individual
in_english.long_meaning: The name Edda, while not directly mentioned in the Bible, is believed to derive from Hebrew and Greek roots signifying beauty and purity. It has been used in Christian tradition to denote someone of remarkable beauty and spiritual purity. The name carries historical significance in European cultures, particularly in Iceland and Germany, where it has been popularized.
